- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Align non-distributed-optimizer gradient-buffer parameter starts to 16 bytes when NVFP4 and fused weight-gradient accumulation are enabled. On the tested SM120 stack, an unaligned `main_grad` causes the TE/cuBLAS NVFP4 weight-gradient GEMM to fail with `CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`; [cuBLAS requires 16-byte alignment for block-scaled FP4 matrices](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cublas/index.html#using-the-cublaslt-api). Existing distributed-optimizer layouts are already aligned; other configurations retain their existing layout.

The failure was observed in GPU training of an eight-layer GDN2 test model with synthetic tokens, TP2+SP and offloading disabled. It is independent of GDN activation offloading. [TE 2.20.2 documents NVFP4 training support for SM100 and SM103](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/transformer-engine/features/low_precision_training/nvfp4/nvfp4.html#supported-devices). Reproduction in a supported training environment is still needed.

## Validation

At current head `66b6bb62a00bdccf8365096e6828215cffed4ce7`, a fresh two-GPU SM120 recheck passes both real TE NVFP4/DDP cases per rank. The cases cover FP32/BF16 gradient buffers, repeated backward passes and cross-rank gradient equality. The control uses parent `9dd63d992a5925dba7f9bfd1aec9dbfb1f54b837` with the identical regression test and unchanged production code; both cases fail on both ranks with `CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`. RHT and stochastic rounding are disabled for exact comparisons.

[Commands, source revisions, original rank logs and audit](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/tree/5af996df67ef2483242ea25be876b996d745449c/nvfp4-current-20261103).

The [earlier evidence](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/tree/02890e97b1273d9a8695f76aaa208730054fe415/gdn-open-issues-20261027) retains layout tests at this head and native GDN2 training controls at their recorded prototype/integration revisions. These results are on SM120; testing on a documented NVFP4 training device remains pending. Upstream GPU CI has not run.

The change addresses the fused weight-gradient output buffer only. A current offload-disabled Qwen TP2+SP baseline also fails in a separate NVFP4 dgrad GEMM; an isolated TE Linear reproduces its width-4112 failure. That is a different failure and is not addressed by this PR.

Black, isort, Ruff, Pylint and the determinism coverage checker passed on the changed files; production code is unchanged in this recheck.

## Issue tracking

Related to #8543.

## Code provenance

No code copied or adapted from external repositories.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests.
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests.
- [x] The real FP4 gradient test checks repeat and cross-rank equality and is registered in the determinism manifest.
- [x] I have added proper typing to the changed code.
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation.
- [ ] I have run the complete autoformatter script.

+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("grad_reduce_in_fp32", [False, True])
+    def test_nvfp4_fused_weight_gradient_alignment(self, grad_reduce_in_fp32):
+        """A small parameter preceding a TE weight must not misalign its main gradient."""
+        te = pytest.importorskip("transformer_engine.pytorch")
+        from transformer_engine.common.recipe import NVFP4BlockScaling
+        from transformer_engine.pytorch.fp8 import check_nvfp4_support
+
+        supported, reason = check_nvfp4_support()
+        if not supported:
+            pytest.skip(reason)
+
+        class Model(torch.nn.Module):
+            def __init__(self):
+                super().__init__()
+                self.linear = te.Linear(
+                    256, 448, bias=False, params_dtype=torch.bfloat16, fuse_wgrad_accumulation=True
+                )
+                self.marker = torch.nn.Linear(2, 1, bias=False, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+            def forward(self, inputs):
+                return self.linear(inputs) + self.marker.weight.sum() * 0
+
+        config = TransformerConfig(
+            num_layers=1,
+            hidden_size=256,
+            num_attention_heads=1,
+            bf16=True,
+            fp4="e2m1",
+            gradient_accumulation_fusion=True,
+        )
+        model = DistributedDataParallel(
+            config,
+            DistributedDataParallelConfig(grad_reduce_in_fp32=grad_reduce_in_fp32),
+            Model().cuda(),
+        )
+        inputs = torch.randn(128, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        recipe = NVFP4BlockScaling(disable_rht=True, disable_stochastic_rounding=True)
+        previous = None
+        for _ in range(2):
+            model.zero_grad_buffer()
+            with te.fp8_autocast(enabled=True, fp8_recipe=recipe):
+                loss = model(inputs).float().square().mean()
+            loss.backward()
+            model.finish_grad_sync()
+            grad = model.module.linear.weight.main_grad
+            assert grad.data_ptr() % 16 == 0
+            assert torch.isfinite(grad).all() and torch.count_nonzero(grad) > 0
+            reference = grad.detach().clone()
+            torch.distributed.broadcast(reference, src=0, group=model.dp_cp_group)
+            testing.assert_close(grad, reference, rtol=0, atol=0)
+            if previous is not None:
+                testing.assert_close(grad, previous, rtol=0, atol=0)
+            previous = grad.detach().clone()
+
     @pytest.mark.skipif(

         reason="Device mesh feature requires PyTorch 2.3 or later",
